hypotheses.justification:
`v` occurs in the statement only through `individualize p v`, and `Refines n (individualize p v).1 p` is still true (and provable) for an arbitrary `v` once `hp : Part.WF n p` is assumed, so `hv` can be dropped.

Why it stays true: by `individualize_cst_eq` (definitional) `(individualize p v).1.cst = setCstFrom c ec (ec - (c+1)) (c+1) p.cst` where `j := p.pos[v]!`, `c := p.cst[j]! = p.cst[p.pos[v]!]!` and `ec := p.cen[j]!`. The junk value of `p.pos[v]!` for `v` out of bounds is `0` (`getElem!_neg` with `default = 0` for `Nat`), so if `v ≥ n` then, because `hp.posSize : p.pos.size = n`, one gets `j = 0`; and if `v < n` then `j < n` by `hp.posLt`. Since the goal `Refines n _ _` starts with an index `i` with `i < n`, `n > 0` in the case that matters (`n = 0` makes `Refines 0 _ _` vacuous), hence `j < n` in both cases. Then `c ≤ j` (`hp.cstLe`), `j < ec` (`hp.ltCen`) and `ec ≤ n = p.cst.size` (`hp.cenLe`, `hp.cstSize`), so `setCstFrom_getElemD` gives, for every `k`,
`(individualize p v).1.cst[k]! = if c+1 ≤ k ∧ k < ec then c+1 else p.cst[k]!`.
Given `k < n` with `p.cst[k]! = k`: if the condition is false the value is `p.cst[k]! = k`; if `c+1 ≤ k < ec` then `hp.cellCst j hj k` (with `p.cst[j]! = c ≤ k`) gives `p.cst[k]! = p.cst[j]! = c`, which together with `p.cst[k]! = k` forces `k = c`, contradicting `c+1 ≤ k`.

How the proof changes: the current proof only uses `hv` to fill the field `IndivData.vLt` so that `individualize_cst_getElemD` (which needs `ec ≤ p.cst.size` via `hd.ecLe`, i.e. `p.posLt v vLt`) applies. That can be replaced by the case split `v < n` (original proof) versus `v ≥ n` (`p.pos[v]! = 0`, so the same computation with `j = 0`, `0 < n` from the target index `i < n`), or by a variant of `individualize_cst_getElemD` that only assumes `p.pos[v]! < n`.

Note: `hp` is *not* removable — it is not implied by the rest. For `n = 3` and `p = ⟨#[0,1,2], #[0,1,2], #[0,2,2], #[3,3,3]⟩` (not `Part.WF`), `v = 0` gives `(individualize p 0).1.cst = #[0,1,1]`, while `p.cst[2]! = 2`, so `Refines 3 (individualize p 0).1 p` fails.
